$comment: The one home for what a risk tier costs (proposal §4.3): which phases run, which human gates hold, whether a run directory opens, and what promotes a change into each tier. Read by .claude/scripts/risk-tier.py (classification + back-fill on promotion), the delivery /add-feature orchestrator (which phases to run) and templates/snippets/run-ledger.md (the run contract). A tier only PROMOTES: risk-tier.py may raise a run's tier at P0, after design (predicted files) or after P6 (the actual diff), never lower it; a user may force a lower tier at P0 only, with a logged reason, and CI re-tiers from the diff (G15). JSON, not YAML, for the reason gates.json gives: the consumers are standard-library python and a hand-rolled YAML subset fails silently.
legacy_tier_note: legacy_tier maps the pack-lane closure verbs (trivial / standard / heavy) a lane skill still names onto the run tiers, approximately: the old trivial (mirrors one sibling) is T1, standard is T2, heavy is T3. T0 had no old equivalent (docs-only changes ran as trivial).
default_feature_tier_why: Decision O3: T2 whenever there is a write path or a UI surface; T1 only when risk-tier.py scores low AND a sibling is mirrored. A feature ask with no signal at all is classified T1 from the text alone and promoted by the first predicted file set that shows a write path, a UI surface or a T3 path.

T0.name: trivial
T0.definition: docs, copy, config with no runtime effect, a typo; no behaviour change

T1.name: low
T1.definition: one module, mirrors a sibling; no new endpoint, write path, external call, dependency, auth, PII or money

lite.P1: ≤5 EARS criteria, every story still carries an IF-THEN clause
lite.P5: acceptance.json + its red tests; no design.md, no test-plan.md

T2.name: standard
T2.definition: new endpoint, write path, external call, new UI surface, new dependency, or a cross-module change

conditional.P4.adr: only for a new primitive or a new dependency

T3.name: high
T3.definition: auth / authz / roles; money movement; PII; tenant isolation; a migration on a populated table; infra / CI; crypto; a breaking public API; a new dependency on a write path; blast radius above threshold
extra: ≥1 property test per SHALL on a money / state invariant
k6 against each QA scenario when a load harness exists
fault-injection test on each new outbound call
release.md with flag / kill switch, migration order and rollback

P6.name: Implementation
P6.writer: implementer (one task at a time); P6b doc-writer

P7.name: Testing
P7.writer: scripts (+ test-engineer for E2E / property tests)

P10.name: Code review
P10.writer: code / test / data / ux / architecture-conformance lenses

human_gates.H1: Intent — requirements.md + quality-attributes.md approved by a human (T3)
human_gates.H2: Contract — design + plan + acceptance.json shown together; approval runs lock-acceptance.sh (T2, T3); plan-critic stands in at T1 and under --yes
human_gates.H3: Irreversible — deploy, IaC apply, migration on a shared database, data deletion, push to a protected branch; typed by a human, never dispatched (any tier)
human_gates.H4: Merge — a human merges; agents never run gh pr merge or approve their own PR (T0+)

blast_radius.why: importers of a touched file in .claude/_graph.json; a change many modules depend on is reviewed like a risky one
